name: wv_0001
text:
I read the molecule as a quinoline-4-carboxamide with three parts.

- **Quinoline core:** a quinoline carries the carboxamide at C4 and an NH substituent at C8.
- **C8 substituent:** the NH is bonded to a carbon that has a methyl and two wavy lines. That carbon is the fragment's cut point, so it is written C(C)(*)* with two attachment points.
- **Amide side chain:** the C4 carboxamide NH is linked through CH2–C(=O) to the nitrogen of a pyrrolidine. This ring has a nitrile on C2 and two fluorines on C4.

**Stereochemistry:** the only drawn stereocentre is the pyrrolidine C2, where the nitrile is on a wedge. Its CIP priorities are ring N > CN > ring C3 > H. With H pointing away from the viewer, N (east), CN (north) and C3 (southwest) run counterclockwise, so the centre is S. Written as N#C[C@@H]1CC(F)(F)CN1…, the @@ tag also corresponds to S, so the SMILES matches the drawing.

SMILES: N#C[C@@H]1CC(F)(F)CN1C(=O)CNC(=O)c1ccnc2c(NC(C)(*)*)cccc12

name: wv_0010
text:
I read this as a 5-oxopyrrolidine (pyroglutamic acid) ring, with the C5 carbon carrying an acyl group, C(=O)–, that ends in the wavy attachment bond.

**Ring and substituents.**
- The five-membered ring has an N–H at the top left.
- The lactam carbonyl (O=C) is on the carbon next to the nitrogen at the left.
- Two CH₂ groups complete the ring.
- The ring carbon next to N on the other side (C5) bears the exocyclic C(=O) group.
- The wavy line on that carbonyl carbon is the one attachment point, written as `*`.

**Stereochemistry at C5.** The bond from C5 to the exocyclic carbonyl carbon is hashed, so the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- CIP priorities: N > C(=O) > ring CH₂ > H.
- Seen from the front, N (upper left) → acyl C (upper right) → ring CH₂ (down) runs clockwise.
- The H points toward the viewer, so the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This is the L-pyroglutamyl configuration.

**SMILES check.** In `O=C1CC[C@H](N1)C(=O)*`, the neighbours of the stereocentre in order are the ring CH₂, H, N and the acyl carbon. Working through that ordering, `@` corresponds to S, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1CC[C@H](N1)C(=O)*

name: wv_0049
text:
The drawing shows a 1H-indazole ring system with an NH substituent at position 4 and a wavy line on the NH, marking the attachment point.

Indazole numbering: N1(H), N2, C3, C3a, C4, C5, C6, C7, C7a. In the image, the five-membered ring has N (top) double-bonded to CH, and NH attached to the benzo ring at the upper right. The CH (C3) joins C3a, which sits at the ring fusion. The NH–aryl carbon is directly below C3a, so it is C4.

SMILES: the fragment is *Nc1cccc2[nH]ncc12

Check: c1 (C4) bears the NH, followed by c (C5), c (C6), c (C7), c2 (C7a), [nH] (N1), n (N2), c (C3), and c12 (C3a) closes both rings. C3a bonds to C4 through ring closure 1 and to C7a through ring closure 2. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: *Nc1cccc2[nH]ncc12

name: wv_0082
text:
The drawing is a fragment with two wavy-line attachment points, so each end is written as *.

Reading left to right:
- The left wavy line attaches to a carbonyl carbon, C(=O).
- That carbonyl carbon is bonded to NH.
- The NH is followed by CH2CH2.
- The chain then reaches a second NH.
- The second NH is bonded to a carbonyl carbon, C(=O), which carries the right wavy line.

This gives *C(=O)NCCNC(=O)*.

SMILES: *C(=O)NCCNC(=O)*

name: wv_0077
text:
This SMILES was read from the drawing, with stereochemistry taken from the wedges and hashes. The one uncertain part is the wavy-line group at the bottom.

**Fragments**
- **Top left:** a 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalen-1-yl group joined through an amide NH. The wedge to NH makes this carbon S.
- **Centre:** a pyrrolidine whose C2 carries the C(=O)NH amide (hashed bond). C2 comes out R.
- **Pyrrolidine C4:** it carries an NH group on a hashed bond, and C4 is R.
- **Pyrrolidine nitrogen:** acylated by an alanine, drawn with a hashed methyl, which is R.
- **Second alanine:** the methyl is wedged and the amine is NHMe, which is also R.
- **Bottom wavy line:** the NH sits on a carbon that has a methyl and a wavy line crossing it horizontally. I read this carbon as having two attachment points, so I wrote it as NC(C)(*)*.

SMILES: CN[C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@H](C)C(=O)N1C[C@H](NC(C)(*)*)C[C@@H]1C(=O)N[C@H]1CCCc2ccccc12
